articles.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
articles.summary: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0. Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln. Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham.
body: Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham.

“We started not the way we wanted,” said Nuno. “We were looking at the situations with hesitation, bouncing balls, too many chances for Southampton to have a second phase, third phase and achieve a goal. But the reaction was good in the second half. The boys fought until the end.”

Richard Kone made an emphatic return to form by scoring a hat-trick inside 15 minutes as QPR thrashed high-flying Swansea 5-0 at Loftus Road. Jimmy Dunne struck twice for Rangers, who were four up at half-time, as the Swans – who were top of the Championship until Friday night – suffered their second defeat in a row. The Welsh side remain second in the table, while QPR’s resounding victory moved them back into the playoff positions in eighth.

articles.title: Burnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom three
articles.summary: Belgian won only one of his 14 games in charge. Relegated Burnley expected to challenge for promotion. Burnley have sacked Nicky Hayen after only 14 games in charge, in the wake of a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left the Clarets in the Championship’s relegation zone.
body: The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October.

Burnley edged past Notts County on penalties in the Carabao Cup in his first match in charge and recovered in the last seven minutes from 2-0 down to draw at home to West Ham in their opening game of the Championship season. However, they then lost badly at West Brom and Norwich, sandwiching a shootout exit from the Carabao Cup at Bradford, and the pattern was set.

Burnley were fancied to push for promotion, which was achieved in their past two Championship seasons, but are now at risk of relegation. Wolves’ come-from-behind win at Turf Moor last weekend left Hayen on the brink and now the club have acted.
A club statement said: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”

articles.title: NFL shutters Paris fan experience as protests overshadow first France game
articles.summary: NFL House and city-center shop closed on Saturday. Paris braces for protests amid heavy police presence. Live: Thousands march in Paris and other French cities. The NFL closed its “NFL House” in Paris on Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts…
body: The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its “OnePass” app, a day after saying its pop-up NFL shop would also be shut on Saturday – in both cases citing “potential accessibility issues”.

Security concerns have overshadowed the NFL’s debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in the league’s first regular-season game in France.
Also on Saturday, the Saints announced that “Saints House has been postponed until Sunday.”
Events planned for Saturday at NFL House included “French Athletes in Football” and “From the Field to the Community”.

articles.title: Spurs boss Ho wants 'more support and training' for WSL referees
articles.summary: Tottenham manager Martin Ho was frustrated by a penalty decision in their defeat by Arsenal and says Women's Super League referees "need more support".
body: A 2-1 win for the Gunners at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday was settled by Alessia Russo's spot-kick in the 56th minute.
Referee Phoebe Cross awarded the decision after Lisa Baum's shot bounced off the post and Cathinka Tandberg's clearance hit Spurs team-mate Ella Morris' outstretched hand.
According to the laws, if the ball hits a hand after it was played by a team-mate, an indirect free-kick should be awarded.
Ho said: "My interpretation of the rule is if your team-mate hits it and your team-mate is one yard away, time and distance is taken into account and it's not a penalty.

articles.title: Brazoswood girls finish as water polo state runners-up with championship loss to Hebron
articles.summary: Brazoswood fell short in its pursuit of a second UIL girls water polo state championship, losing to Lewisville Hebron 10-8 in Saturday's Class 6A final at Josh Davis Natatorium in San Antonio.
body: The Buccaneers finished their season 32-3, with all three losses coming against Hebron, which finished 28-0 and captured its first state title. Brazoswood previously lost to the Hawks 8-6 and 9-5 during the regular season.
Coached by Robert Brown, the Buccaneers were making their fifth consecutive state tournament appearance and seeking their first championship since winning the 2024 title.

Saturday's final featured six ties, and neither team led by more than two goals at any point during the match. Brazoswood pulled within 9-8 on a goal from senior attacker Larissa Bracken with 4:15 remaining, but Hebron sophomore attacker Lauren Waggoner scored with 2:41 left to provide the final margin.
Hawks senior goalkeeper Amber Cho was named the championship game's most valuable player after making 13 saves and helping Hebron keep Brazoswood scoreless over the final four minutes of the contest.

articles.title: Donnarumma & Guehi highlight Man City issues as solid Arsenal move level
articles.summary: Manchester City's 100% winning start to the Premier League season comes to an abrupt end against Aston Villa - leaving Enzo Maresca with glaring defensive issues to resolve.
body: Nicolas Jackson's double in a 2-1 home win for Villa means City have now managed only one clean sheet in their past six games and the form of goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and defender Marc Guehi is of concern.
Since the start of last season, only eight players have made more errors leading to Premier League goals than Donnarumma and Guehi with three each.

City's most recent shutout came in their impressive victory at Liverpool two weeks ago but, around that game, City have conceded against teams ranging from Champions League holders Paris St-Germain to top-flight strugglers Sunderland.
Maresca was forced to try different combinations at the back against Villa, but as the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson once said, "attack wins you games, defence wins you titles".

articles.title: Tottenham boss Martin Ho says WSL refereeing ‘has got worse’ after derby defeat
articles.summary: Tottenham Hotspur head coach Martin Ho has said the standard of refereeing in the Women’s Super League “has got worse”. Ho’s side lost 2-1 in the north London derby on Saturday after Arsenal were awarded a controversial second-half penalty which proved to be the winning goal.
body: In the 56th minute referee Phoebe Cross deemed Ella Morris to be guilty of handball after team-mate Cathinka Tandberg’s clearance struck her arm. Alessia Russo duly converted from the spot.
The Premier League and WSL are following new guidance this season in line with International Football Association Board (IFAB), the independent guardians of football rules.

They state: “A handball offence is not committed when a player: is hit on the hand/arm by the ball which has been played by a team-mate (unless the ball goes directly into the opponents’ goal or the player scores immediately afterwards, in which case a direct free kick is awarded to the other team).”
Speaking in his post-match press conference, Ho said: “They (the officials) can’t give me an explanation. I think it’s got worse, the refereeing has got worse than it was last year.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta slams Arsenal’s ‘terrible’ schedule after Everton win as Bukayo Saka faces up to 12 games out
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta hit out at Arsenal’s ‘terrible’ schedule after his much-changed side beat Everton 2-0 to draw level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.
body: Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 on Saturday, with centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes both on target, but Arteta was far from happy with the fixture list. His side had travelled to Nottingham Forest last Sunday and drew 2-2 with Bayern Munich on Wednesday night before the 3pm kick-off, and he made five changes as a result.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Arteta said: “Yes we’re very happy with the victory, with the performance and with the week, because we were given a terrible schedule. Sunday afternoon, then Wednesday night in Munich, coming here really late on Thursday and having to play again in the Premier League against a really tough opponent on Saturday at 3pm. We have overcome every hurdle, on top of some injuries, and I love the mentality of the team and the quality that we’ve shown today.”

The victory came without Saka, who was forced off inside 10 minutes in Munich after feeling something at the top of his leg. Speaking before the Everton game, having seen the results of the winger’s scan, Arteta said: “I think it will be weeks, the extent of the injury, I think we’re going to have to repeat the scans in a week, ten days to see the extent of that.”

articles.title: Giant Sequoia stakes Classic claims in Futurity
articles.summary: Giant Sequoia produced an eyecatching performance to win the William Hill Futurity Trophy at Doncaster and in the process virtually guarantee Aidan O’Brien the trainers’ championship.
body: Aidan O'Brien looks to have another Classic contender on his hands as Giant Sequoia bounced back to form with an emphatic success in the Group One Futurity Trophy at Doncaster.

It was stablemate Sergei Diaghilev who set a brisk pace at the head of the Group One field, before the race began to take shape as they hit the two-furlong pole, with all the runners on the stands side.

Ryan Moore and favourite Noble Exhibit put down their challenge a furlong and a half out, but Giant Sequoia (11-1) was travelling strongly upsides and really picked up when asked by Dylan Browne McMonagle, stretching three lengths clear of Andrew Balding's staying-on Gran Dia.
It was a record-extending 13th success in the race for O'Brien, who had been happy to draw a line through the winner's disappointing effort in last month's National Stakes.

articles.title: Oklahoma State announces student crackdown after fans injure marching band members
articles.summary: Oklahoma State is moving the Cowboy Marching Band to a new section of Boone Pickens Stadium for Saturday’s homecoming college football game against Colorado after fans in the student section hurt two band members with thrown cans and water bottles.
body: The two students were injured, and instruments were damaged during the Cowboys’ 42-28 win over UCF on Oct. 10, according to a letter from Brent A. Marsh, the university’s vice president for student affairs. Four students have had their All Sports Passes permanently revoked.

Marsh’s letter described a problem that stretched beyond one afternoon. “At recent games, fans in the student section have thrown cans and water bottles, some of them aimed at the Cowboy Marching Band,” Marsh wrote. “It is dangerous and it is hurting people.”

The injuries overshadowed a win that moved head coach Eric Morris’ team to 4-1. Oklahoma State, then ranked No. 18, led 24-21 entering the fourth quarter before a field goal, an Evan Jackson defensive touchdown and a touchdown pass from quarterback Drew Mestemaker to receiver Wyatt Young put the game away.
Fellow students criticized the behavior. “I thought you can drink, have a good time without throwing your bottles at the band,” Oklahoma State freshman Cason Tulous said.

articles.title: Preston claim first point under Alexander
articles.summary: Substitute Aune Heggebo struck late for West Brom to deny Preston a first win under Graham Alexander in a 1-1 draw at a wind-swept Deepdale in the Championship.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and West Bromwich Albion at Deepdale on Saturday; Graham Alexander earns his first point as Lilywhites boss.
The Norwegian came off the bench on the hour and rifled home an 82nd-minute leveller just four minutes after Andrew Hughes hooked North End into the lead from a corner.
James Morrison's visitors had already come from behind to win against Wrexham and Blackburn in their last two matches but Preston deserved their point.

It was their first since Alexander took charge earlier this month and came at the end of a week where two of their first-team coaches left the club, in part as a result of their position at the bottom of the Championship.
